# `Path`

[Back to stdlib index](../stdlib.md)

Ipe.Path — typed, validated filesystem paths.

`Path` is opaque: the ONLY way to build one is `fromString`, which
normalises the path and REJECTS a NUL byte or a `..` traversal escape.
Because a `Path` is validated at construction, the helpers (`base` / `dir`
/ `ext` / `isAbsolute`) and every `Ipe.File` entry point take a `Path`, not
a raw `String` — an unvalidated string can never reach a filesystem syscall.
Use `Ipe.File` for the effectful side (read / write / exists).

Compose paths with `under root child`, never by string concatenation: it
refuses an empty, absolute, or NUL-bearing child, and checks that the
result lies component-wise below the root (`/repo2/x` is not under
`/repo`). A child cannot climb out through `..`: `fromString` folds an
in-bounds `..` (`a/../b` is `b`) and refuses one that escapes.
`absolute` resolves a relative path against the working directory
through the same join (it needs the `filesystem` capability).

Symlinks: `under` and `absolute` are lexical. They never touch the
filesystem, so they neither follow nor forbid a symlink; a joined path
whose ancestor is a link can still reach outside the root when opened.
Confining a program against links is the capability jail's job, not
this module's.

## `fromString`

```ipe
fromString : String -> Result Error Path
```

`fromString raw` — the parse-don't-validate seal: the only `Path`
constructor. Normalises separators and returns `Err` when `raw` contains a
NUL byte or escapes its root via `..`; otherwise `Ok` the cleaned `Path`.

## `toString`

```ipe
toString : Path -> String
```

`toString path` — recover the cleaned path string.

## `base`

```ipe
base : Path -> String
```

`base path` — the final path component.

## `dir`

```ipe
dir : Path -> String
```

`dir path` — everything but the final component.

```ipe
ext : Path -> String
```

`ext path` — the file extension (with the dot), or "".

## `isAbsolute`

```ipe
isAbsolute : Path -> Bool
```

`isAbsolute path` — does the path start from the root?

## `under`

```ipe
under : Path -> Path -> Result Error Path
```

`under root child` — join the relative `child` beneath `root`. Returns
`Err` when `child` is empty or absolute, or the join would not lie below
`root`; otherwise `Ok` the cleaned joined `Path`. A `child` built by
`fromString` never holds a `..` that escapes, so `a/../b` joins as `b`.
On Windows, a `child` element containing `:` (a drive or an alternate data
stream), made only of dots and spaces (which Windows strips to `.` or
`..`), naming a reserved device (`CON`, `NUL`, `COM1`, `nul.txt`, ...), or
ending in a dot or space (Windows strips it to another name) is refused too.

## `absolute`

```ipe
absolute : Path -> Task Error Path
```

`absolute path` — resolve `path` against the working directory. A path
rooted with its own volume is returned re-sealed. On Windows, a path rooted
without a volume (`\x`) takes the working directory's volume, and is refused
when the working directory names no complete volume. A relative path is joined beneath the
working directory with `under`, so it inherits every refusal (including a
drive-relative `C:x`). A working directory that is not UTF-8 is refused.
